title: SECTION II — DREAM, WAKEFULNESS AND BLENDED TIME
summary: This section brings the book’s dream motif into everyday life. Dream, sleep and memory mingle with social satire, technology, caste, labour, ritual, village forms, modern roads, fear, identity and death. The result is deliberately unstable: intimate recollection, folk vocabulary and civic observation repeatedly cross the border between waking fact and dream logic.

entries.title: Before the Dream
entries.summary: A meditation on body & consciousness, language & meaning and earth & natural imagery. The recurring register of mirrors and seeing helps carry the poem’s movement. Further reading (from the passage beginning at PDF p. 85; printed p. 84): The mother’s use of mustard and chillies against the evil eye places protective ritual inside an intimate relationship. The poem makes fear and care visible together: a parent tries to act against a danger that cannot be confidently located or controlled. Reading the scene does not require treating affection as proof of the ritual’s efficacy. Its human pressure comes from the wish to protect a child when reassurance alone is insufficient.

entries.title: Fortunate
entries.summary: A meditation on body & consciousness, society & power and dream & wakefulness. The recurring register of body and breath helps carry the poem’s movement. Further reading (from the passage beginning at PDF p. 86; printed p. 85): Convalescence and the need for support make dependence tangible. Crutches and other people’s assistance challenge any picture of a wholly self-sufficient individual. The poem also directs attention toward the distance between cultivated understanding and conduct: acquaintance with principles is not the same as living by them. Good fortune can therefore be read through the presence of practical fellowship, measured by what people do when another person cannot manage alone.

entries.title: Alas, Kumarila!!
entries.summary: A meditation on faith & sacred life, body & consciousness and freedom & liberation. The recurring register of body and breath helps carry the poem’s movement. Further reading (from the passage beginning at PDF p. 96; printed p. 95): The journey for medical care brings a philosophical dispute into contact with an inconvenient, painful body. Travel, delay and access to a doctor test what public provision means in practice; the language of free treatment sits uneasily beside the speaker’s experience of obtaining it. Arguments about causation do not occur outside this setting. The juxtaposition makes thought answerable to ordinary need, while the doctor’s examination supplies a bodily scale against which grand explanations are tested.

entries.title: Beyond the Index and Table of Contents
entries.summary: A meditation on home & belonging, earth & natural imagery and knowledge & reason. It moves from language & meaning toward home & belonging, allowing the poem’s emphasis to change as it develops. Further reading (from the passage beginning at PDF p. 99; printed p. 98): Fibres, a loom and the intelligence of craft challenge the assumption that knowledge is exhausted by its written arrangement. Skills depend on practice and on people who transmit them through shared work. The poem does not make books useless; it questions the completeness of an index as a map of understanding. Its place in this carefully catalogued volume creates a useful tension: the reader must follow the entry beyond its heading toward the life that gives it substance.
